name: Synchrotron light
description: An accelerated charge radiates, and the particle loses the energy it radiates. In a magnetic field it circles, radiates on every turn and slowly spirals inwards: synchrotron radiation, the reason electron rings need constant re-acceleration. Without radiation this particle could never reach the centre. Put a magnet on the axis so that it radiates fast enough to get there in time: the radiated power grows with the square of the field. Switch the map to 'particle field' to watch the radiation leave.

reality.represents: Synchrotron radiation damping: a circling charge spirals in

remarks.detail: The particle radiates as Larmor's formula says and loses that energy (the Landau–Lifshitz force), exact in classical electrodynamics while the loss per turn is small.

Its charge to mass is chosen so that it radiates 0.1 % of its energy per turn at modest speed. A real electron this slow would radiate almost nothing; real synchrotron light comes from electrons with γ in the thousands, beamed forward.
Electron rings replace the lost energy with RF cavities every turn; here nothing does, so the orbit shrinks.

remarks.line: A coil is one thin loop
remarks.detail: The coil is a single loop of thin wire carrying a steady current, its field the exact Biot–Savart field (perpendicular to the plane in it, and far from uniform); a real magnet has many turns, iron and pole pieces shaped for a uniform field.
